thread:
Maya Patel: Quick decision thread: final approach for marketplace artifacts + partner-distributed kernels for 'Gaia-Large-v3'. Two choices: A) upload full quantized bundle to marketplace, or B) publish a small signed runtime stub + manifest and host kernel packs behind authenticated partner URLs. Need final call and license wording for exceptions.
Diego Alvarez: Vote B. Marketplaces prefer small artifacts; hosting kernels behind partner-auth reduces upload failures. We should include kernel_hashes in manifest so partners can verify.
Quinn Li: Agree with B. Also propose a signed flag in the manifest: 'kernels_hosted_externally': true and 'auth_url_expiry': 7d. That helps marketplaces accept a small payload.
Aria Singh: HW partner asks to ship an appliance image that contains the quantized artifact. Legal: will this count as redistribution?
Sasha (Legal): If partner embeds the packaged, quantized runtime inside an appliance image, that is allowable under a limited redistribution clause — provided we add audit rights, an export-control screening, and a one-time exec exception approval. Raw checkpoint redistribution remains prohibited. I'll draft a short addendum clause: "Partner may embed integrated, quantized runtime artifacts in appliance images subject to audit and export-control review; distribution of raw model checkpoints is prohibited without Redwood written consent."
Maya Patel: Ok, B + legal addendum. Diego/Quinn implement manifest schema with kernel_hashes and signed auth URLs. Sasha to draft addendum and exception workflow. Diego please confirm marketplace upload limits and map which clouds require full bundle vs stub.
deploy-bot: created test artifact gaia-v3-q4-stub-20240610, manifest signed.
Maya Patel: Thanks team — I'll post the PR-safe blurb once legal shares the addendum. Follow-up sync 06/11 for signoffs.
